svg.aria-label: Two NISAR passes are combined into an interferogram and a coherence map; after removing ionosphere, troposphere and tides, each dam site is compared with a ring of ground around it and reported only if quality checks pass
svg.text: What the pipeline does with two NISAR passes
This example uses synthetic data. Each tile shows the same area around one dam site, at 5 m resolution.
Comparing each site with its surroundings
The dam site (solid circle) is compared with the ground around it
(dashed ring). Errors that affect both equally, such as the reference
level and broad atmospheric effects, cancel out.
Checks before a result is reported
Coherence at the site is high enough.
Phases around loops of three dates add up.
The result does not depend on the reference area.
Passing sites are reported with their uncertainty.
Failing sites are flagged and not reported.
The tiles are illustrative. They were generated from a synthetic 2 cm dip beneath several fringes of ionospheric and atmospheric delay.
